alerts.title: Rising creatinine and declining eGFR on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for patients on TDF. Creatinine has steadily risen from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), with eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m². TDF is a known cause of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome. Urinalysis shows protein 1+, which may indicate TDF nephrotoxicity. Evidence against drug attribution: no costovertebral angle tenderness, stable weight, and no oedema. However, the progressive trend over 6 years strongly suggests TDF-related renal toxicity. Occasional ibuprofen use (2–3 times weekly) may compound renal risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate for TDF-induced nephrotoxicity. Consider substituting TDF with ABC or alternative per guidelines. Avoid nephrotoxins including ibuprofen. Refer for renal assessment.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for this visit despite abnormal renal findings requiring action. Guidelines require screening for developing signs and symptoms at every visit for patients on ART. The rising creatinine, low eGFR, and proteinuria necessitate a documented management plan including potential regimen review and renal referral.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment addressing renal function decline. Create a plan for TDF review, renal evaluation, and ibuprofen cessation. Schedule follow-up labs.

alerts.title: Ibuprofen use with renal impairment on TDF
alerts.message: Patient takes ibuprofen 400 mg 2–3 times weekly for headaches. With eGFR at 52 mL/min/1.73m² and rising creatinine on TDF, concurrent NSAID use increases risk of further renal injury. TDF guidelines list chronic kidney disease and acute kidney injury as major toxicities. Ibuprofen may accelerate renal decline in this already compromised patient.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to discontinue ibuprofen. Recommend paracetamol for headache relief. Monitor renal function closely if NSAID use cannot be avoided.

alerts.title: Fatigue may signal TDF lactic acidosis
alerts.message: Guidelines list exhaustion or extreme fatigue as a presenting sign of TDF-associated lactic acidosis or severe hepatomegaly with steatosis. Patient reports mild fatigue over 2 months. Evidence for drug attribution: fatigue is a recognized TDF toxicity and patient has been on TDF for 3 years. Evidence against: patient attributes fatigue to work schedule, and no muscle cramps, abdominal pain, or decreased appetite are reported. Given concurrent renal impairment, this symptom warrants further evaluation.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform LFTs and RFTs as recommended for suspected TDF toxicity. If deranged, evaluate for lactic acidosis and consider regimen substitution.
